Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G2980; mute:--dumb.
BiblicalUsage: Three times in Mark, and always about a mouth that will not open. A father brings a boy with a dumb spirit that tears him and throws him down; Jesus rebukes it, and the boy speaks. And the crowd marvels at a different healing, that He makes the deaf to hear and the dumb to speak.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for a sealed mouth carries no theology of its own; its weight is the two healings, that the same Christ who casts out the spirit also opens the ears and the tongue.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
